title: Console Communication Error
shortDescription: Console lost communication with motor controller.
fullDescription:
E1 on Sole Fitness treadmills (F63, F65, F80, F85) indicates the console and motor controller aren't communicating. Most cases are wiring related — pinched or unplugged data cable inside the upright.

Reseat the 8-pin console cable at both ends. If still failing, measure continuity on the cable.

faq.a: Very common — always reseat after relocating.

title: Speed Sensor Fault
shortDescription: No speed feedback from front roller sensor.
fullDescription:
E2 means the reed-switch/optical sensor monitoring front roller RPM isn't producing pulses. Either the magnet fell off or the sensor unplugged.

Reseat the sensor on its bracket — it should be within a business-card width of the magnet.

fixSteps.title: Inspect sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove motor hood; verify sensor connector and magnet on front roller.

title: Safety Key Not Installed
shortDescription: Safety key is missing from console.
fullDescription: E3 or a key icon means the safety magnet isn't detected. Seat the key, or if it's already installed, the reed switch may need replacement.

faq.a: Yes — many magnetic keys are interchangeable.

title: Incline Motor Error
shortDescription: Incline motor not responding to position command.
fullDescription:
E4 means the incline motor did not reach its target position within the time limit. Try incline calibration from the engineering menu first.

If calibration fails, the incline motor or its pot/limit switch is bad.

fixSteps.title: Calibrate
fixSteps.instruction: Engineering mode (hold Stop+Speed+Incline); run incline calibration.

title: Motor Current Overload
shortDescription: Motor drew too much current — controller safety shutdown.
fullDescription:
E5 on Sole units is an overcurrent fault. Deck friction is the top cause — a belt that needs lubrication can spike motor amps by 2-3x.

Lubricate, and if E5 persists, check motor brushes on higher-end models.

fixSteps.title: Lubricate deck
fixSteps.instruction: 100% silicone lube under belt; distribute at 2 mph.

title: Motor Controller Overheat
shortDescription: Motor control board temperature exceeded safe threshold.
fullDescription: E6 usually means the MCB's MOSFETs are getting too hot — often from poor ventilation or heavy use. Let the treadmill cool 30 minutes; ensure the motor compartment vents aren't blocked.

fixSteps.title: Cool & vacuum
fixSteps.instruction: Let cool 30 min; vacuum motor compartment to remove dust.

faq.a: Underside of motor hood — don't block.

title: Overspeed Fault
shortDescription: Actual speed exceeded commanded speed — possible control fault.
fullDescription:
E7 indicates the motor is running faster than commanded — often because of a stuck speed command or a mis-reading sensor reporting bad data.

Usually corrects itself after power cycle; recurring E7 means MCB service.

title: Console Memory Fault
fullDescription: E8 indicates saved settings could not be read. Perform a factory reset from the engineering menu.

title: Input Voltage Fault
shortDescription: AC input voltage out of acceptable range.
fullDescription:
E9 indicates the MCB detected input voltage too low or too high. Extension cords, loose outlets, or shared circuits often cause this.

Plug directly into a dedicated 15A outlet.

fixSteps.title: Use dedicated outlet
fixSteps.instruction: Plug directly into wall outlet (15A dedicated).

title: Lubrication Reminder
shortDescription: Time to lubricate deck — informational only.
fullDescription: LUB is a maintenance prompt. Apply 100% silicone lube between belt and deck, then reset counter from engineering menu.

fixSteps.title: Lubricate
fixSteps.instruction: Apply silicone under belt; walk at 2 mph to spread.

faq.a: Some models claim so, but manual lube is still recommended.
